question: Tariffs and quotas in the trade issues are used to ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**protect domestic companies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Tariffs and quotas are trade policy tools used by governments to restrict imports.

• They help protect domestic companies by making imported goods more expensive or limiting their quantity.

• These measures are often used to support nascent industries in the country that are not yet able to compete with established foreign competitors.

• By protecting domestic industries, tariffs and quotas can help maintain jobs and economic stability within the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tariffs**

• A tariff is a tax imposed by a government on imported goods and services.

• Tariffs raise the price of imported goods, making them less attractive to consumers compared to domestic products.

• They are used to protect domestic industries from foreign competition and to generate revenue for the government.

• **Quotas**

• A quota is a government-imposed trade restriction that limits the number or value of goods that can be imported or exported during a specified time period.

• Quotas help to control the volume of trade between countries, ensuring that domestic industries can compete effectively.

• Quotas can be applied to specific products, industries, or countries.

• **Trade Protectionism**

• Trade protectionism refers to government actions and policies that restrict or restrain international trade.

• The goal is to protect local businesses and jobs from foreign competition.

• Common protectionist measures include tariffs, quotas, and subsidies.

• **Economic Stability**

• Economic stability occurs when an economy experiences constant growth and low inflation.

• Trade protection measures can help maintain economic stability by supporting domestic industries and employment.

• However, excessive protectionism can lead to inefficiencies and higher prices for consumers.
